title: White House announces infrastructure and investment projects in Mississippi
excerpt: The administration reported new federal grants for transportation and private sector investments across the state.
bodyHtml:
The White House announced on October 26, 2026, a series of infrastructure projects and private investments in Mississippi. The administration awarded a $44 million grant to expand the I-55/I-69 corridor in DeSoto County from four to ten lanes.

The Mississippi Export Railroad received up to $35.5 million to modernize and automate a 121-year-old swing bridge and upgrade track. Additionally, the administration awarded $51.1 million in federal BUILD grants to improve U.S. Highway 80 in Brandon, expand truck parking along I-10 in Hancock County, and upgrade Mallett Road in D’Iberville.

Private sector developments include a $20 billion investment from xAI to build a data center in Southaven and a $12 billion investment from Amazon to expand data center operations in Madison County. Siemens Energy is investing $300 million to build a manufacturing facility in Pearl, while BWC Terminals is investing $316 million to locate a terminal facility in Pascagoula.
